history.summary: A two-deity temple at Hampankatta in central Mangaluru, housing Lord Shiva as Sharabeshwara (west side of the complex) and Lord Mahaganapathi (south side); the idols are covered in silver sheets. The name 'Sharavu' derives from 'Shara' (arrow): legend says the Tulu king Veerabahu accidentally killed a cow with an arrow meant for a tiger, and on the advice of Sage Bharadwaj performed penance - building a tank to the north (Sharatheertha), erecting a cow statue to the south, and installing a Shivalinga (Sharabeshwara) at the spot where the cow fell. The temple grounds retain the tank and a stone idol of the sacred cow. NOTE: the claimed ~800-year antiquity is legendary and UNVERIFIED; no dated inscription is cited in consulted sources. The temple is a hub of cultural events such as Yakshagana and dance drama alongside daily worship.

town_description: Mangaluru (formerly Mangalore) is a major port city on the Arabian Sea coast of Karnataka, the administrative headquarters of Dakshina Kannada district and the heart of Tulu-speaking Tulunadu. Known for its beaches, banking and education institutions, and diverse cuisine, it is also a temple city whose ancient shrines anchor the region's religious life.
